pass_a_gloss: §15 dual gloss (Armenian-via-French sense) ≠ Pass B running English. Theme: Law of the tree: immortality kept or mortality if transgressed.
pass_b_english: But so that the human being might not think himself too great and swell with pride, as if he had no master; so that, in his relations with God his creator, he might not mistake the power and liberties given him by overpassing the bounds set for him; and lest, flattering himself in proud thoughts, he should revolt against God — a law was given him by God, to teach him that he has a master, the Lord of all things.

And he set him certain limits, so that if he should keep the commandment of God he should always remain as he was — that is, immortal; but if he should not keep it, he should become mortal and be dissolved into earth from which his formation had been taken. ([[dust you are >> Bible:Gen 3:19]])

Now the commandment was this: ‘Of every tree that is in the Paradise you shall freely eat; but of that tree alone from which is the knowledge of good and evil, of it you shall not eat; for in the day you eat, you shall surely die.’ ([[Gen 2:16-17 >> Bible:Gen 2:16-17]])
